``` → This captures input *only in-browser* (no data stored/sent), making it harmless. 3. **Add Clear Disclaimers** - Banner at top: “⚠️ EDUCATIONAL DEMO ONLY — NO REAL AUTHENTICATION OR DATA STORAGE” - Include a “Why this matters” info panel explaining phishing red flags. 4. **Supplement with Learning Materials** - Pair the demo with a guided exercise: “Spot 5 inconsistencies in this page vs. the real SecureBank site.” - Use browser dev tools to show URL spoofing, lack of HTTPS, mismatched certificates, etc. 5. **Alternative (Recommended): Use Existing Safe Platforms** - [GoPhish](https://getgophish.com/) (open-source, designed for authorized phishing simulations — requires proper setup & governance). - [KnowBe4](https://www.knowbe4.com/) or [Cofense](https://cofense.com/) — enterprise platforms with built-in compliance safeguards. - [OWASP Juice Shop](https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/) — vulnerable web app *for learning*, includes phishing-related challenges. 🚫 **What NOT to Do:** - Don’t clone real login pages (e.g., Gmail, Microsoft) — risks trademark violation & accidental misuse. - Don’t collect, store, or transmit real credentials — even “anonymized.” - Don’t run without written approval from your organization’s legal/IT security team. 💡 Pro Tip: Focus the lesson on *detection*, not deception — e.g., “Here’s how to verify a URL,” “How to inspect a certificate,” “Why ‘https://secure-bank-login.net’ isn’t trustworthy.” Let me know if you'd like a ready-to-run local demo (HTML + instructions), guidance on setting up GoPhish safely, or a slide deck outline for training — happy to help responsibly.
